transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I've been struggling lately, but what really scared me enough to make this appointment is... I keep having these thoughts. I just keep thinking it would be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes, when I'm driving home from the clinic, I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just... didn't turn the wheel at a curve. It's really frightening me.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up or wondering about the consequences of not turning the wheel while driving?
It's been going on for about a month now. We recently took in a relative, and it's just been this intense up-and-down crisis ever since. That's really when these thoughts started happening.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do over the past month?

No, I really haven't. I just... I haven't even touched my camera lately. I haven't checked the bird feeders with any real interest, or cared at all about what's coming up in the garden. It's actually kind of frightening to me, honestly, because doing those things... that used to be how I felt like myself. And now I just don't have any interest in them.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before these thoughts started?

Yes, my energy has definitely changed. It's just... completely gone. At work, just walking from the treatment area over to the lab benches feels like I'm dragging myself through mud. And by the time I get home, I can barely even make dinner or help with the evening care routine. I'm just so exhausted all the time.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep?

Yes, my sleep has been pretty bad. I either just lie awake at night, replaying everything I’ve done wrong, or I wake up way before dawn and I'm already exhausted. Even when I try to stay in bed longer to get more rest, it doesn't really help. I just... I don’t feel rested enough to go for a run or even function normally during the day.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Yes, I'm pretty sure I've lost a few pounds. My appetite has been... well, kind of all over the place. But lately, I mostly just pick at a piece of toast or have some coffee in the morning. Then I'll get to the end of a long clinic shift and suddenly realize I’ve barely eaten anything all day. I just really don't have much interest in food right now.
Have you felt like you're moving slower than usual or like you're restless and can't sit still?

I don't think so. I know I mentioned feeling like I'm dragging at the clinic because I'm just so exhausted, but I don't feel like my body is actually moving in slow motion or anything. And I'm definitely not restless. I really don't have the energy to be pacing around or fidgeting. Honestly, if I have the chance to just sit still in a chair, that's exactly what I do.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about yourself or things you've done?

Yes, a lot, actually. I just keep telling myself that I’m a terrible person... mostly for resenting the disruption at home. I just, I replay every impatient look I've given or every sharp comment I've made in my head. It really just feels like proof that my husband and the rest of the family would be better off without me.
Do you feel like these thoughts of not waking up or wondering about the consequences of not turning the wheel are something you can push away or control when they happen?

I'm not really sure what you mean about the wheel... I haven't had any thoughts about driving off the road or crashing my car, if that's what you're asking. When I say they'd be better off without me, it's mostly just a heavy feeling of guilt. I don't actually sit there wishing I wouldn't wake up or planning to do anything like that. So I guess I don't really have those specific kinds of thoughts to push away.
Do you feel like these thoughts and feelings have been constant, or are there times when you feel somewhat better?
I'm not really sure. I haven't noticed any times where I feel much better, honestly. It... it just feels pretty constant right now. I just wake up feeling this way and it stays with me all day.
Would you say these feelings of guilt and worthlessness are present nearly every day?

Yes, it's pretty much every day. Like I said before, I just keep telling myself I'm a terrible person because I resent the disruption at home. I replay every impatient look or sharp comment I make, and it just feels like proof that my husband and the family would be better off without me. It's just a constant weight I carry around with me all the time.
Have you experienced any periods of even slight improvement in your mood over the past two weeks?

No, not really. I haven't noticed any breaks in it at all over the last couple of weeks. It's just been exactly like I described... just heavy and constant every single day. I don't think there's been any improvement, even a small one.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness and guilt are interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home?

Yes, they definitely are. I've actually started making mistakes at the clinic, which isn't like me at all. And I've been avoiding my friends lately because I'm afraid I'll either snap at someone or just completely fall apart in front of them. At home... my husband has had to take over pretty much everything. He's doing the bills, making all the meals, and just... having to keep me safe when the thoughts get really dark.
Do you feel like you're unable to do things because your body feels heavy, or like you're moving more slowly than you should be?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I feel exhausted all the time, but my body doesn't actually feel physically heavy, and I don't think I'm moving any slower than usual. It's more just... a complete lack of energy and drive to get up and do things, rather than feeling like I'm moving in slow motion.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt even slightly better than the others?

No, like I mentioned a little bit ago, there really haven't been. Every single day has been exactly the same. I haven't had any days where I woke up feeling even a little bit lighter... it's just been that same constant low across the board.
Do you feel like you're fidgeting or restless, or do you feel like you're stuck in one place and can't seem to get moving?

No, I don't think I'm fidgeting or pacing around or anything like that. And I'm not physically stuck, like I said before... I just don't have the energy to want to move or do anything. It's not a physical restlessness or being frozen in place, it's just... I'm just sitting there because I don't have it in me to do anything else.
Have you felt like you're fidgeting or unusually restless?

No, like I just mentioned a second ago, I haven't felt restless or fidgety at all. I really don't have that kind of nervous energy right now. It's just... I'm too drained to move much, but I'm definitely not pacing around or feeling antsy.
Have you felt like you're moving slower than you usually do?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, when I actually do get up to do something, I think I move at a normal pace. It's not like I'm moving in slow motion or anything... I just don't get up very often because I'm so drained. But the actual moving itself doesn't feel slower.
Do you feel like you're fidgeting or unusually restless?
Doctor, I think you just asked me that. No, I'm not fidgeting or restless. Like I said, I just don't have the energy for that kind of movement.
Do you think these feelings of sadness and guilt are severe enough that you're unable to experience any pleasure at all?

Yes, I think so. I just don't get any joy out of anything anymore. I haven't even touched my camera in weeks. Usually, I'm out checking the bird feeders or looking to see what's coming up in the garden, but lately... I just don't care. I look at them and feel nothing. It's honestly a bit frightening, because doing those things used to be how I felt like myself, and now there's just no interest at all.
